summary: Introduces a narrow shared Web/Feishu lifecycle authority after reproduced generic-shell self/shared-service kills: models still decide whether a restart is useful, while physical restart authority becomes generation-bound to an operator-published exact deployment, durable action receipts, a dedicated service_control tool, a cross-process lifecycle lease, and pre-stop desired-state verification.

components.owning_subsystem: shared LFL Web/Feishu service lifecycle control, exact deployment identity, and generic-shell effect fencing
components.disposition: ADMIT as a new narrow mechanical lifecycle authority that replaces generic execute_command's implicit ability to control shared Web/Feishu while reusing restart_mirror.sh as the sole physical stop/start executor. The model retains the decision whether to restart; PID, cwd, shell approval, and manifest observations do not grant lifecycle authority.
evidence: A real Web session durably executed managed Web/Feishu SIGTERM calls as ordinary successful execute_command receipts, proving the ownership gap was physical authority rather than WAL loss.

TDD locks literal and wrapped managed-PID kills, restart/direct-launch paths, dynamic PID sources, stale generations, durable accepted-before-worker ordering, exact desired roots, and readonly noninterference.
A cross-process test proves desired-deployment publication waits for the lifecycle lease while a physical restart window is active, closing the check-to-execute race.

The first full repository gate rejected new ambient os.environ copying; the implementation was corrected to a minimal deterministic control environment without expanding the environment-access baseline.
components.verification_level: TDD RED/GREEN plus 180-test adjacency, cross-process lifecycle-lock qualification, runtime-env ratchet, whole-tree security, Ruff/Pyright, bash syntax, and full repository ci_gate
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: The model can observe desired deployment generation/roots/head/artifact identity, per-service live PID identity, accepted/running/succeeded/failed action receipts, restart receipts, binding mismatch details, Web readiness and Feishu heartbeat. Missing desired state or binding mismatch fails before stop; stale generation fails before worker spawn; stale worker binding durable-fails instead of executing an old plan. Program code does not infer whether a restart is semantically desirable.
components.rollback_route: Revert the P0-A code; no application-data/provider/model schema migration is required. For operational rollback while P0-A is active, publish the prior qualified code root as the next desired generation and restart through the same control plane rather than decrementing generation.

g1.necessity: Shared Web/Feishu services serve multiple sessions and are not session-owned execute_command jobs. A reproduced normal Web session successfully signalled those shared services through generic shell, so a separate mechanical lifecycle authority is necessary to prevent one task from physically terminating the shared runtime while preserving ordinary shell capability.

g2.authority_owner: new generation-bound shared-service lifecycle control plane backed by operator-published desired deployment; existing restart_mirror.sh remains the sole physical stop/start executor
g2.non_duplication: The new authority replaces generic shell's implicit shared-service lifecycle control rather than creating a second physical restart implementation. PID/per-service manifests remain observations only, restart_mirror remains the physical executor, and model reasoning retains the semantic decision whether to request restart.

model_evidence: operator-published desired deployment id/generation/code root/runtime root/exact Git SHA/WebUI artifact SHA
per-service Web/Feishu live manifest PID and process identity observations
restart receipt and explicit binding mismatch details
existing Web readiness, logs, Feishu heartbeat, and queue/processing facts
g3.recovery_or_reason: Missing desired deployment or a root/SHA/dirty/artifact mismatch fails before stopping a healthy service. A stale expected generation rejects before worker spawn. If deployment identity changes after acceptance, the worker durable-fails instead of executing an obsolete plan; cross-process lifecycle locking prevents publication from racing an already-running physical restart. Status/read-only observations remain available so the model/operator can choose a new publish, retry, or rollback generation explicitly.

g4.rollback: No application-data migration is introduced. Revert P0-A to restore the prior tool surface, or while P0-A is active publish the prior qualified code root as the next monotonic desired generation and restart through the same control plane. Existing desired/action/per-service-manifest files can remain inert operational evidence for older code.
